search_overall: Beam search is strongest at low budgets, but its advantage shrinks as compute increases.
At matched cost, extra lookahead usually gives less benefit.
search_difficulty: Extra search can hurt easy questions, help medium difficulty questions, and still fail on the hardest ones.
Both question difficulty and compute budget should guide the search setting.
search_adaptive: At low budgets, 16 generations nearly match best-of-N with 64.
Predicted difficulty loses some of its advantage at higher budgets.
revision_quality: Revision improves single-answer accuracy, then the gains level off.
Sequential sampling slightly beats independent sampling with either selection rule.
revision_mix: At high budgets, a mixture can beat either pure parallel or pure sequential generation.
Easy questions favor long chains; harder questions often benefit from more independent starts.
The best mix depends on both difficulty and budget.
revision_adaptive: Adaptive revisions keep improving after parallel sampling begins to plateau.
64 candidates can beat parallel best-of-N with 256 candidates.
model_comparison: Extra inference often wins on easy or medium questions, especially when expected inference use is low.
A larger model is often better on very hard questions or when expected inference use is high.
r_example: The better choice depends on both question difficulty and expected use.
